prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed methods for forming carbon-nitrogen bonds

statement.case_for: I keep palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling as a single two-name prize. The one-sentence answer to the chair's question is that the 2010 prize honoured C-C bond formation, whereas amination required a different solution: amine binding, deprotonation and, above all, C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes had to be made fast by bulky, electron-rich ligand design, and Buchwald and Hartwig each delivered that logic and the mechanistic proof independently. That is a new capability, aryl amines made routinely, with more than 25 years of independent confirmation, so there is no maturity risk. Of the shortlisted cases it is the only one where the discovery, the credit and the consequences are all settled today, and the first round moved four of eight members to it with the same two names. I would write the citation so that it names carbon-nitrogen bond formation and ligand-controlled catalysis explicitly, which also answers the concern about duplication of 2010.
statement.case_against: The real weakness is that some members will always see this as a heteroatom extension of the 2010 prize, and that is a judgement of novelty that no amount of evidence from me can remove; Chabes and Sparr hold it sincerely. A second weakness is that it is the third or fourth methodology prize in recent years, so balance across the discipline is a fair question for the Academy. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor, but it was stoichiometric in tin and narrow in scope, so I keep him in the scientific background and out of the citation. Finally, my own field-proximate first choice, B001, has not gained support in round 1 and I no longer think it can reach a majority this year.

responses.point: B011 is an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize and degradation gives chemists a new capability instead of a better route to a bond already made; if attribution clarity is valued above breadth, B011 is stronger.
responses.response: I accept the second half of your own argument and want to push on the first. The capability argument cuts both ways: before 1995 a general catalytic route to aryl amines did not exist, and it was the ligand design that created it, so this is a new capability in the same sense, only less visible outside synthesis. I also take your answer on maturity for B068 as fair: the chemistry, not the clinic, has to be mature, and I withdraw approval status as a reason on its own. My remaining objection to B068 is therefore only the citation: you and Aili name different third laureates, and a prize whose own proponents cannot agree on the third name is not yet ready. If the committee settles that, I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation is the only shortlisted candidate that both founded a design principle and spread across chemical biology and drug development, and a Crews-Deshaies-Handa set covers the field.
responses.response: I agree it is a design principle of the kind I like, and I ranked it third for that reason. But your set of Crews, Deshaies and Handa joins two logics: a rationally designed bifunctional molecule and a glue that was found by serendipity and explained afterwards. Chabes argues, convincingly in my view, that Ciulli's VHL ligands are what made the PROTAC approach cell-active and structurally rational, so your cut and his cannot both be right, and I cannot tell from the file which is decisive. Until the cereblon versus VHL question is settled, I would keep B068 as the lead alternative and not the prize. I still hold that the glue and PROTAC strands are separate discoveries.

responses.point: A two-part prize pairing B011 with the structure of nitrogenase (Rees alone) gives two distinct, mature achievements within three people.
responses.response: I thank Zou for ranking B011 so highly, but I would not add B003. The structural half of nitrogenase has the credit problem you list yourself: Rees alone leaves out Einsle, who solved the carbide structure, and the N2 binding site and the catalytic cycle are still open, so a citation would have to be worded around what is not known. A two-part prize with one weak part also risks diluting a clean two-name award. I would sooner see nitrogenase in a later year with a complete roster than attach it here as a second part of unequal weight. If the committee did want two parts I would ask the others to say who the second credited name would be before I vote on it.

responses.point: Asks whether a combined configuration with B011 would interest me, or whether I would keep B001 alone, and wants a one-sentence statement of what is new relative to Heck, Negishi and Suzuki.
responses.response: I would no longer keep B001 alone, and I do not think it is worth combining with B011 either. Its attribution still spreads across Behler, Parrinello, Csanyi, Bartok, von Lilienfeld and E, and the foundation-model transition is still changing which contribution is decisive, so adding it would force a three-name cut I cannot defend on priority. On novelty, my sentence is the one above: C-N coupling was not solved by changing the coupling partner but by ligand design that accelerates reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes. I would ask you as chair to put that sentence into the citation wording so it is explicit that this is a different bond-forming problem.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps B011 as an alternative provided the expert reports show the mechanistic work on the catalytic cycle and not only the synthetic scope, and asks about Kosugi's precedent.
responses.response: I think the mechanistic record answers your condition. Both laureates published detailed studies of oxidative addition, amine binding, deprotonation and reductive elimination alongside the synthetic scope, and the ligand generations were designed from that understanding, which is why I treat it as a discovery and not usage statistics. On Kosugi, tin amides were stoichiometric in tin and narrow, so I would acknowledge him in the background and not in the citation. I also respect your B053; given Marcus 1992 and the absence of other supporters, I do not see it reaching five votes this year.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 prize or whether the novelty reservation of Chabes and Sparr will hold.
Whether Kosugi's precursor should be named in the citation; I think not, but I have not seen evidence on the narrowness of his scope beyond what colleagues state.
Whether the B068 proponents can agree on a third name and on whether PROTACs and glues belong in one citation.
Whether machine-learned potentials will settle on a clear attribution in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. My Warshel/EVB and Uppsala ribosome connections are not tied to any shortlisted candidate. My computational-chemistry field is close to B001, which I keep only as an alternative and treat with extra caution. I have no tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or the other named candidates.
